---
title: "An irreducible fraction"
date: 2026-11-03
categories: [Number Theory]
source: "IMO 1959 P1"
difficulty: 1
---

Prove that the fraction $\dfrac{21n + 4}{14n + 3}$ is irreducible for every natural number $n$.

::: {.hint}
A common divisor of two numbers divides every integer combination of them.
:::

::: {.hint}
Find integers $a, b$ with $a(14n+3) + b(21n+4)$ not depending on $n$.
:::

::: {.solution}
Let $d = \gcd(21n+4,\, 14n+3)$. Then $d$ divides
$$
3(14n+3) - 2(21n+4) = 42n + 9 - 42n - 8 = 1,
$$
so $d = 1$ and the fraction is already in lowest terms.
:::

This was the very first problem of the very first International Mathematical Olympiad, held in Romania in 1959.
